advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Extend the empty-orphan adopt test so `origin` also carries init scaffolding (matching production) to prove the `--allow-unrelated-histories` adopt does not abort on overlapping root dot-files.
evidence: test_sync_narrow_refspec.py:137-138 origin built with `_new_tickets_repo(origin)` then `_commit_event(origin, ...)` only — no scaffolding committed
test_sync_narrow_refspec.py:142 local built with `_commit_scaffolding(tracker)` — only the local side has the dot-files
test_sync_narrow_refspec.py:153-156 assertions only check the origin ticket dir exists and origin_sha is an ancestor; no assertion that scaffolding files with differing content merge without conflict
advisory.finding: The empty-orphan adopt test does not reproduce the production shape: its `origin` carries only a ticket event and NO init scaffolding, while a real shared tracker carries `.gitignore`/`.gitattributes`/`.pre-commit-config.yaml`/`.store-compat.json` at root just like the orphan. The add/add scaffolding overlap that a real adopt would face is therefore never exercised, so the test cannot catch an adopt that aborts on a scaffolding conflict.
scenarios: Adopting a shared tracker that also carries init scaffolding at root (the normal production case).

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Verify the empty-orphan `--allow-unrelated-histories` adopt does not abort on add/add conflicts of scaffolding root files (.gitignore/.pre-commit-config.yaml/.store-compat.json) when their content differs, and add a merge=ours/-X ours strategy or a driver covering those paths if it can.
evidence: init.py:61-68 `_GITATTRIBUTES` only contains `.bridge_state/* merge=ours` — no driver for `.gitignore`, `.gitattributes`, `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, `.store-compat.json`
sync.py:181-186 on non-zero merge `_git(tracker, "merge", "--abort")` then warns and keeps local — so an add/add conflict on scaffolding aborts the adopt

A real orphan store from init.py AND the shared tracker both commit these same-path root files (init.py:515-538 commits `.gitattributes`); an `--allow-unrelated-histories` merge treats identical paths on unrelated sides as add/add, resolving cleanly only when byte-identical.
dropped.finding: The empty-orphan adopt path union-merges two unrelated histories that both carry the same init scaffolding root files (.gitignore/.gitattributes/.pre-commit-config.yaml/.store-compat.json), but only `.bridge_state/*` has a `merge=ours` driver. If those scaffolding files differ in content between the orphan and the shared tracker (e.g. across rebar versions), the `--allow-unrelated-histories` merge hits an add/add conflict on a path with no merge driver, `_union_merge` aborts and keeps the empty local orphan, so the store silently fails to adopt and keeps reading `[]` — the exact symptom the fix targets.
scenarios: Fresh single-branch clone whose init produced an empty orphan store, adopting a shared tracker whose scaffolding files were written by a different rebar version (different .pre-commit-config.yaml / .store-compat.json content).
